The Governors of the 19 Northern states have dissolved the Board of Directors of the New Nigerian Development Company, jointly owned by the states, as part of efforts to reposition the company and strengthen its operations. The decision was taken on Tuesday at a Special General Meeting in Kaduna by the Secretaries to the Governments of the 19 Northern states, who represented their respective governments as shareholders. The shareholders resolved that a new board would be constituted, subject to the adoption of the relevant ordinary resolutions at a duly convened general meeting and compliance with statutory requirements. Addressing journalists after the meeting, the Secretary to the Gombe State Government, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, said the shareholders had agreed to undertake a comprehensive reorganisation of the company to improve its performance and restore confidence in its administration. He said the exercise was aimed at strengthening the company’s institutional capacity, improving corporate governance, enhancing operational efficiency and repositioning it as a viable investment and development institution serving the collective economic interests of the 19 Northern states. According to him, the composition, nomination and appointment of the new directors would reflect the ownership interests of the participating states, the company’s Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the provisions of the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. Njodi further disclosed that the incoming board would review the existing management structure, personnel, administrative arrangements, operational framework and overall performance of the company. He said the exercise would enable the new board to strengthen the management structure and promote accountability, professionalism and improved corporate performance. The incoming board would also conduct a comprehensive corporate governance, financial, administrative and operational audit of the company, he added. According to Njodi, the audit would cover NNDC’s financial position, assets and liabilities, existing investments, subsidiaries, joint ventures and other commercial interests. Godwin Isenyo
